title: Russia Strikes Kyiv Railway Depot in 6th-Straight-Night Barrage, Killing 12 Including 6 Rail Workers
detail: Russian forces attacked Kyiv and its suburbs overnight into September 1 with ballistic missiles, Kalibr cruise missiles, S-300/Banderol munitions, and 218 drones (roughly one-third jet-powered) — Ukraine's air defenses intercepted or suppressed 199 of the 199+ targets, striking 28 locations with debris falling at 10 more. A ballistic missile tore through a Ukrzaliznytsia railway maintenance depot in Kyiv, killing 6 rail workers and destroying a workshop. In Brovary, east of Kyiv, a separate strike killed 4 and injured 13, damaging a five-story residential building. Across Kyiv city and oblast, the overnight barrage killed at least 12 (8 in the city, 4 in Brovary/oblast) and injured 21. It was the sixth consecutive night of sustained Russian bombardment of the capital region, coinciding with Ukraine's first day of the new school year.

title: Putin Calls Zelensky's Airline Warning 'State Terrorism' After Zelensky Says Russian Airspace No Longer Safe
detail: President Zelensky told foreign airlines and insurers that the 'safe moments' in Russian airspace were over, warning that Ukrainian long-range drones would keep targeting Russian military and war-supporting infrastructure and effectively closing Russian skies to civilian aviation. Speaking at a press conference on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan on September 1, President Putin called the warning 'a bid for state terrorism,' saying 'we don't negotiate with terrorists' and that Moscow would 'find a way to respond' if the threat resulted in civilian tragedies. Shares in Russia's national carrier Aeroflot fell 5.11% on the Moscow Exchange following the exchange, though European and U.S. carriers already avoid Russian airspace while Chinese, Turkish, UAE, and Gulf carriers continue operating despite the risk from drone strikes and recurring airport closures.
